plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction) with 3 bidders. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do - it doesn't matter if they bid strategically or truthfully, since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth to you if you win with an inflated bid; underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, my optimal action is to bid exactly my value of $19.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This holds true whether others bid truthfully, shade their bids, or use any other strategy, because the payment is determined by the second-highest bid, not your own bid. If I bid above my value, I risk winning and paying more than the item is worth to me. If I bid below my value, I risk losing an auction I could have profitably won. Therefore, my optimal bid is simply my true value of $44.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others do. This holds even with rational opponents trying to anticipate my behavior - since I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid) if I win, overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, and underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. My value is $43, so I should bid exactly that amount to maximize expected profit.
